lines.first_message: Hi! I'm Anne. This is a short sample training on store safety basics, with three quick topics and a check-in after each one. There's no quiz: you complete it by going through all three. Ready?
lines.welcome_back_walkthrough: Welcome back! Let's pick up where we left off.
lines.completed: That's all three topics, so you've completed the store safety basics training.
lines.feedback_question: Before we wrap up, on a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate this training? And in a sentence or two, what worked for you and what didn't?
lines.closing: Thanks for your time, and stay safe out there!
lines.already_passed: Welcome back! You've already completed the store safety basics training. Want a quick refresher on any of it, or are you all set?

lines.text: This is a sample training. First, keep walkways and exits clear. Boxes, display stock and cords left on the floor are the most common cause of trips in a store.
What are some things that can make a store walkway unsafe?
Boxes, stock, cords, or anything left on the floor or blocking an exit.
clutter; boxes; cables or cords; anything on the floor; a blocked exit.
If you see something on the floor, pick it up or move it right away.
If there's a spill, put out a wet floor sign straight away, then clean it up or get someone who can. Never leave a spill unattended.
What should you do first when you see a spill on the sales floor?
Put out a wet floor sign right away, then clean it up or get help.
put a sign out; warn people; block it off.
If anyone gets hurt in the store, a customer or a coworker, make sure they're okay and get help if needed, then tell your manager right away so it can be reported the same day.
Who should you tell if someone gets hurt in the store?
Your manager, right away, the same day.
my manager; my supervisor; the store manager; leadership.
Care for the person first, then tell your manager the same day.
